newsitem.title: FRANCE: French police swoop on Moslem militants.
newsitem.headline: French police swoop on Moslem militants.

text.p: Police hunting for clues to a bomb on the Paris underground railway arrested about 20 suspected Moslem fundamentalists in pre-dawn raids in the Paris region and northern France on Thursday, police sources said.
Reporters at the Paris headquarters of criminal police saw several handcuffed people taken in for questioning. Officials declined to comment on their identity.
Sources close to the investigation said the swoops were part of the hunt for leads on a December 3 bomb attack on a Paris underground train which killed four commuters.
Police have twice raided Islamist circles since the blast, but all 23 people detained were later released.

The latest raids also appeared linked to a shadowy gang, some of whose members converted to Moslem fundamentalism, which was blamed for robberies in northern France. Four members of the gang were killed in a shootout with police last year.
Police suspect Moslem guerrillas linked to Algeria carried out the Port Royal underground station attack, which closely resembled a wave of bombings that killed eight people last year.
Meanwhile, police confirmed that alert security guards at a central Paris store had stopped three men of suspected North African origin handling a gas canister with nails and bolts last weekend.
Gas containers filled with explosives, nails and screws were used in this month's and most of last year's attacks.
The three men fled the clothing store in the busy Opera district. Police said the cyliner contained no explosives or detonator but bags of nails and screws were found nearby.
A police spokesman said detectives were not sure whether the incident was linked to terrorism.
Security measures have been drastically stepped up in the underground railway network and department stores for fear of more attacks during the busy Christmas shopping period.
